question.text: A daily wage worker without PAN wants to start investing in mutual funds. He can save Rs. 1,000 per month. What is the best advice for him?

answer.text: He cannot invest in mutual funds without PAN under any circumstances
He should first earn enough to obtain PAN and then start investing

He can start a Micro-SIP of Rs. 1,000 per month using PEKRN/KYC with alternate photo ID, as long as the total annual investment per mutual fund — composite of Micro-SIPs and lump-sum investments — does not exceed Rs. 50,000 per investor per year
He must invest through a corporate or trust account instead

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI allows Micro-SIP / small-investment route without PAN, subject to the Rs. 50,000 limit per investor per year per mutual fund. The limit is composite, covering the small investor's Micro-SIP and lump-sum investments together. The investor still completes KYC through a SEBI-registered KRA, typically via PEKRN with an alternate photo ID such as Aadhaar / voter ID. Rs. 1,000 per month works out to Rs. 12,000 per year, comfortably within the per-mutual-fund limit. The Trap: The limit is per mutual fund (per AMC), not "across all mutual funds", and it is a composite limit — additional lump-sum investments at the same fund count toward the same Rs. 50,000 cap. Note: Source: NISM Series V-A (Mutual Fund Distributors) workbook, pp.194-195 — Micro-SIP / small-investment PAN exemption with PEKRN/KYC and alternate photo ID; composite Rs. 50,000 limit per investor per year per mutual fund.
